scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A thin layer of cream stops sunburn on a blazing day. How does sunscreen fight the sun?

scenes.name: uv
scenes.text: Sunlight carries ultraviolet rays. UVB mainly burns the skin, and UVA goes deeper and ages it.

scenes.name: mineral
scenes.text: Mineral sunscreens use zinc oxide or titanium dioxide, which mainly absorb UV, and scatter some of it.

scenes.name: chemical
scenes.text: Chemical filters absorb UV energy and release it as a tiny amount of heat.

scenes.name: spf
scenes.text: SPF measures protection against UVB. SPF thirty blocks around ninety seven percent, when applied properly.

scenes.name: broad
scenes.text: Broad spectrum, or a PA rating, means it also protects against UVA.

scenes.name: reapply
scenes.text: It wears off with sweat and water, so reapply about every two hours outdoors, and use enough.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Absorb, scatter, reapply. Follow for more on how things really work.
